html:
Italian Libya was the North African colony that Italy took from the Ottoman Empire in 1911. On the 1920 and 1930 maps it covers the coast and the desert behind it.

Italy invaded in the Italo-Turkish War, and the Ottomans gave up the provinces of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica in 1912. Holding them was harder. In Cyrenaica the Sufi order of the Senusiyya led a long guerrilla war, with the teacher Omar Mukhtar as its field commander.

Under Mussolini the army crushed the revolt. Much of the population of the Cyrenaican plateau was forced into camps, where many thousands died. Omar Mukhtar was captured and hanged in 1931. In 1934 the two provinces were joined as Libya, and Italian farmers were settled on the coast.

British and Axis armies fought across Libya in the Second World War, and Italy lost it by 1943. Italy gave up its claim in 1947, and Libya became independent in 1951; see Libya.
sum: Italian Libya was the North African colony that Italy took from the Ottoman Empire in 1911. On the 1920 and 1930 maps it covers the coast and the desert behind it.
